page: Amazon Web Services r8gd.16xlarge is a memory-optimized server powered by custom AWS Graviton processors. Built on the ARM64 architecture with Neoverse-V2 cores, this instance features 64 dedicated physical cores running at 2.8 GHz with a 1:1 thread-to-core ratio. The hardware configuration includes 512.0 GB of RAM, providing 8.0 GB of memory per core, alongside 3800 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 30 Gbps.

Benchmark results highlight exceptional memory and multi-core performance. The server achieves top-tier memory bandwidth, reaching 7396.42 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 464.12 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. Multi-core capabilities are strong, as evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 25367.0 and a Passmark CPU physics test score of 15962.8. Database and caching performance are also highly competitive, with Redis SET operations reaching 134.09 million operations per second and Passmark database operations scoring in the top tier. However, single-core performance and text generation for very small language models represent relative performance tradeoffs.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the r8gd.16xlarge offers high resource density by combining high-capacity memory with fast local NVMe storage on an energy-efficient ARM64 architecture. This profile makes it highly suitable for memory-intensive and storage-heavy workloads. Recommended applications include high-throughput databases, in-memory caching layers like Redis, large-scale software compilation, and multi-threaded data processing tasks.
